sources.title: RFC 5545 iCalendar
sources.version_or_commit: RFC 5545, September 2009, with R02/R03 for verified errata
sources.governing_conditions: UID is TEXT and identifies the component; RECURRENCE-ID defaults to DATE-TIME, matches master value type/local form, and identifies the original slot. EXDATE wins over RRULE/RDATE inclusions; duplicates collapse; an unsynchronized DTSTART/rule is undefined. INTERVAL is positive and defaults to 1. COUNT includes DTSTART; COUNT and UNTIL are mutually exclusive; UNTIL for TZID DATE-TIME DTSTART is UTC DATE-TIME and is inclusive. Missing recurrence fields derive from DTSTART. A matching VTIMEZONE must cover recurrence instances. Folds use the first instant; gaps use the preceding offset. DTEND gives exact recurrence duration; DURATION gives nominal duration, with day/week components differing across transitions. §3.2.20 preserves unknown VALUE-type data; generic readers may ignore extension properties. New VEVENTs need UID/DTSTAMP and, without METHOD, DTSTART.
sources.applicability: Governs the offline interchange design. Product subset, raw-byte preservation, upsert keys, tombstones and UI input rejection are product decisions. The earlier skip-gap text must be read with R03 and the later computed-time paragraph.
sources.observation: Independent read-only HTTP retrieval and semantic inspection of relevant surrounding primary context; no downloaded code executed.

sources.title: RFC 5546 iTIP
sources.governing_conditions: VEVENT CANCEL is an organizer scheduling notice to affected attendees. UID identifies a series; cancelling one instance requires RECURRENCE-ID, while whole-series cancellation omits it. The cancellation sequence increases; message/component and attendee constraints govern the transaction.
sources.applicability: A useful analogy for original-slot addressing; its notification and organizer obligations do not turn offline snapshot editing into an invitation cancellation.

sources.title: Microsoft Graph event resource
sources.governing_conditions: originalStart is DateTimeOffset in UTC for a recurring occurrence/exception, not a single instance. seriesMasterId is a String. Read-only type distinguishes singleInstance/occurrence/exception/seriesMaster. cancelledOccurrences holds occurrenceId strings on a master and requires $select/GET master ID. exceptionOccurrences needs $select/$expand on the master; exception and instance relationships omit cancelled instances. Event ID can change on a container move unless the ImmutableId preference is used.
sources.applicability: Comparator only: provider IDs and UTC field shape do not replace UID/typed RID. Retrieval selectors are conditions on provider diagnostics; no Graph integration is proposed.

sources.title: Microsoft Graph update event
sources.version_or_commit: Graph REST v1.0 PATCH live documentation
sources.governing_conditions: PATCH updates the event object at its ID. Outlook recurrence exceptions cannot move to/before the previous occurrence day or to/after the next occurrence day; the API can return HTTP 400 ErrorOccurrenceCrossingBoundary. Updating a master with multiple attendees and separately modified instances can emit separate notifications.
sources.applicability: Confirms the provider-specific restriction. It cannot be used to forbid an otherwise legal file-only move across a date boundary; the final keeps this distinction.

claims.claim: No future/range edit or iTIP message
claims.condition_and_applicability: RANGE affects multiple occurrences; METHOD:CANCEL is organizer/attendee scheduling. Neither is the requested single offline operation.
Resolve file TZID to preserved matching VTIMEZONE covering the series; derive UTC instants rather than fix weekly UTC; no host-zone fallback.
First fold occurrence; imported/generated gaps use pre-gap offset; invalid dates still ignored. Rejecting a new entered gap destination is explicitly product policy.
Master DTEND implies exact recurring duration; DURATION retains nominal form (day/week components can vary elapsed length); existing override explicit form/meaning retained.

claims.claim: Weekly grammar default and end constraints
claims.condition_and_applicability: WEEKLY, positive INTERVAL default 1, at most one matching BYDAY; optional COUNT xor UNTIL, COUNT includes DTSTART, TZID DTSTART UNTIL UTC DATE-TIME. Missing end bound is unbounded.
